content.thinking: This looks like a classic config-induced failure: a deploy at 23:44 changed the Redis port to 6380 instead of 6379, tanking the cache hit ratio to zero and spiking p50 latency, with the affected endpoint being redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380. I'm now weighing whether to model the state transition as the port change itself or use the deploy revision hashes as the from/to states, with the subject tied to the cache service.

hypotheses.subject: redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380
hypotheses.summary: The deploy at 23:44:00Z changed the summary-cache endpoint to redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380, a port nothing is listening on. Every cache lookup is refused, cache_hit_ratio collapses from ~0.9 to 0 and p50 latency jumps from ~26ms to ~190ms as requests fall through to the slow path.

supporting_evidence.claim: ERROR io-shop: summary cache lookup failed - connection refused to redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380 (185 of 200 requests)
ERROR io-shop: summary cache lookup failed - connection refused to redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380 (200 of 200 requests)

hypotheses.subject: 0d8e826225f0de73958a8a8dd3d867b2ae249e72
hypotheses.summary: Alternatively the deploy shipped changed code (not merely configuration) whose cache client targets the wrong port or mishandles the cache path; rolling back the revision 0d8e826225f0de73958a8a8dd3d867b2ae249e72 would restore service either way.

supporting_evidence.claim: p50 latency and cache_hit_ratio depart from baseline in exactly the deploy minute: 2026-09-22T23:44:00Z,0.01,188,200,202,1200,453890394,2147483648,1790077744.112329,0.075

hypotheses.subject: cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local
hypotheses.summary: Alternatively the Redis cache io-shop depends on went down or stopped listening at that instant, and io-shop merely reports the refused connections; the coincidence with the deploy would then be accidental.
